paths.description: Requested member host redirect and public homepage, representing the entry/navigation/login gateway.
Primary authentication template, including password/passkey choices and blank-submit recovery.
Primary account-opening journey entry and choice state.
Deliberately invalid route representing HTTP error and recovery state.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: Dark emulation leaves the complete homepage white/red and the probe reports colorScheme="normal"; no system-driven dark theme is applied.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `color-scheme: light dark` and theme surfaces/text with `light-dark()` or `prefers-color-scheme`.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-contrast / forced-colors: controls, text and scrollbars remain visible under high-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a failing color-contrast audit on the homepage; no forced-colors/high-contrast adaptation was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet WCAG contrast minimums and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations for essential controls.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: The CSS/runtime probe found no View Transition usage while navigation and content state changes are instant full-page swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route/state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: The first viewport is dominated by two promotion bands, category chips, a full-width campaign hero and five more campaign tiles before core informational content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce duplicated promotional chrome and prioritise the login/account action and core service content.

findings.summary: Layout adapts to narrow viewports with no horizontal overflow and no fixed pixel widths forcing a desktop layout on mobile; viewport meta present; fluid scaling and intrinsic sizing rather than brittle breakpoints.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport Chrome lays out a 1280 CSS-pixel page at 0.28125 scale; layout reports no viewport meta and the page is a shrunken desktop canvas. Login behaves the same.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid width=device-width viewport and rebuild key templates with intrinsic, fluid layouts that reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero container-query rules, and reused header/login/promotion components remain desktop-sized under a narrow viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable components containment and size-aware `@container` adaptations instead of relying on a fixed desktop canvas.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails target-size on both homepage and login; the shrunken desktop UI makes controls especially small on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Use at least 24x24 CSS-pixel targets with spacing, preserve visible focus, and provide non-hover paths.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse homepage performance is 0.15 with LCP 17.3s and TTI 34.6s; the controlled trace was faster (LCP 1.87s), showing severe variability.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, remove redirect latency, defer non-critical work and monitor field LCP/INP/CLS.

findings.summary: No cumulative layout shift from late content (images, banners, fonts) that arrives without reserved space.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout observation records CLS 0.173 with a 0.170 shift; 87 of 100 audited images lack dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/banner space with dimensions or aspect-ratio and stabilise late campaign/font insertion.

findings.summary: The main thread is not blocked by long tasks or heavy scripting; work is deferred, chunked, prioritised, or moved off-thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 6.1s main-thread work and 3.4s JavaScript execution; trace still finds two long tasks and 48ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary script, split long tasks and schedule non-critical work by priority.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: HAR records 227 requests/3.28MB, seven parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets, blocking scripts, redirects and missing cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse critical CSS, defer scripts, fix cache headers and shorten dependency/redirect chains.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 648KiB unused JavaScript and 111KiB unused CSS; HAR shows 65 scripts and 1.80MB script transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage to remove unused/duplicate bundles and load feature and analytics code conditionally.

findings.summary: Interactive elements have accessible names, correct roles, and form fields have labels; images have alt text where meaningful; canvas/expressive content is exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails multiple ARIA/name rules and image-alt; the image audit finds 44 missing alts, and login also fails form labels/link names.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair accessible names/roles, label all controls, and provide meaningful or explicitly empty alt text.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports insufficient foreground/background contrast on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground and surface tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: Homepage has an empty H1, no main landmark, malformed list/ARIA structures and 206 apparently unnamed anchors; login also lacks a main landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide one meaningful H1/main landmark, logical headings/lists, valid ARIA and a tested keyboard focus sequence.

findings.summary: Text is legible and inclusively rendered: comfortable line layout, precise alignment, stable rendering across mixed fonts, no clipping or cramped wrapping that harms comprehension.
findings.evidence: The 360px capture shrinks a 1280px desktop canvas to 28%, making body text and controls too small to read comfortably.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow instead of scaling; use readable responsive type, line length and spacing.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: Both audited templates omit a viewport meta tag, Lighthouse fails meta-viewport and target-size, and narrow rendering does not reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow user scaling, set width=device-width and ensure content reflows without loss at narrow/zoomed conditions.

findings.summary: The page loads without console errors or uncaught exceptions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports browser errors logged to the console on both homepage and login.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove uncaught/runtime and failed-resource errors, and enforce clean-console smoke tests.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: Although doctype/UTF-8 are valid, Lighthouse finds incorrect image aspect ratios and the image audit finds 87 missing dimensions and 95 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare intrinsic image dimensions/aspect ratios and modernise responsive asset markup.

findings.summary: The page uses the platform cleanly: no deprecated APIs, no avoidable BFCache blockers, no broken source maps or inspector issues, no stale vulnerable libraries, no paste-prevention on inputs, and no notification/geolocation prompts on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a deprecated API, inspector issues, BFCache blockers on login and substantial legacy/unused code.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated APIs and BFCache blockers, resolve DevTools Issues and update stale dependencies.

findings.summary: The page has a unique, descriptive <title> and a meta description.
findings.evidence: Homepage metadata is descriptive, but the primary login template has no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unique, accurate meta description to the login and every indexed template.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Raw content is crawlable, but both homepage and login omit viewport metadata and Lighthouse fails mobile viewport/link-name checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add mobile viewport metadata and ensure all links have descriptive accessible text and real hrefs.

findings.summary: Where the page represents an article, product, organization, event, place or other rich entity, structured data and share-preview metadata accurately describe the visible content.
findings.evidence: Homepage has Open Graph tags but no JSON-LD despite representing a financial-services organization; the account page has placeholder description "Site Description".
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/FinancialService JSON-LD and complete share metadata on key templates.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS/HSTS are present, but CSP and nosniff are absent; 5 cookies are not Secure and all 14 sampled cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and nosniff, then mark every HTTPS cookie Secure and use the least-permissive SameSite value.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture finds 42 third-party origins and five known tracker families; HAR attributes 122 requests and 1.78MB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and remove non-essential trackers, gate optional analytics on consent, and minimise/batch retained telemetry.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: The main response lacks clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy as well as CSP; only HSTS is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP including frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and nosniff; evaluate Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive authenticated surfaces.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: Public pages set lang=ja, but the separate account-opening application has no document language; no explicit direction is set.
findings.suggestedFix: Set the correct lang on every application/template, add direction support and prefer logical CSS properties.

findings.summary: Forms prevent and recover from mistakes humanely: validate after interaction (not prematurely), give clear required-field feedback, announce errors accessibly, and signal invalid fields visibly rather than blaming the user.
findings.evidence: Submitting the visible login form empty produced no invalid controls, alert role or visible error message; login inputs are not required.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after submit/interaction, focus and announce a concise error summary, and mark invalid fields with accessible inline guidance.

findings.summary: Input is assisted, not obstructed: correct autocomplete tokens so address, payment, sign-in and sign-up fields autofill, and inputs are highlighted/sized to help the user rather than trip them up.
findings.evidence: Login ID has no autocomplete token and password uses generic autocomplete="on" instead of username/current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password while retaining the passkey option.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 95 use legacy formats, 58 lack srcset, 39 below-fold images are not lazy and 8 are oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP responsive sources, lazy-load below-fold media and right-size decorative assets.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: The load starts 227 requests including 52 fetch/XHR requests and many duplicate advertising destinations before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or eliminate non-essential background fetches and analytics until intent/consent; batch remaining telemetry.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 1.78MB; Google Tag Manager/destination scripts alone dominate the largest transfer list while campaign imagery adds substantial decorative weight.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce third-party/media budgets, defer campaign media, and remove redundant tag destinations.

findings.summary: Heap size and DOM node count are reasonable for what the page is; the footprint is proportionate rather than bloated.
findings.evidence: Baseline snapshot has 719,381 nodes and 39.1MB self size, growing to 723,804 nodes/39.8MB after repeated scrolling; this is heavy for a public landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce DOM/script/third-party populations and set memory/DOM budgets for the public shell.
